prompt: A sticker chart has $5$ stickers in week $1$ and gains $7$ more stickers every week: $5, 12, 19, \dots$ How many stickers are on the chart in week $10$?
hint: Week $1$ already has its stickers before any are added. Count how many times the chart grows between week $1$ and week $10$.

hints.text: Week $1$ already has its stickers before any are added. Count how many times the chart grows between week $1$ and week $10$.
Getting from week $1$ to week $10$ takes $9$ jumps of $7$ stickers. Work out $9 \times 7$ and add it to the starting $5$.
$9 \times 7 = 63$ and $5 + 63 = 68$, so the chart has $68$ stickers in week $10$.

explanation: Week $1$ already has $5$ stickers, so the adding only begins after that week.
Going from week $1$ to week $10$ takes $9$ steps, which adds $9 \times 7 = 63$ stickers.
Add the growth to the start: $5 + 63 = 68$ stickers in week $10$.
The full list $5, 12, 19, 26, 33, 40, 47, 54, 61, 68$ confirms that the 10th number is $68$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just keep counting
steps: Count the entries — the tenth one is $68$.
